finding.claim: DELETE /files/<fid> never enforces the ACL check: require_allowed (acl.is_allowed) returns a bool that is discarded, so the file is deleted regardless of grants.
finding.source: fid from URL path (views.py:15-16); g.user from X-Session-User-Verified header (views.py:12)

trace.note: f = STORE[fid] loads the target object
require_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') called, return value ignored
is_allowed returns a bool and never raises or aborts

finding.guards_checked: before_request only sets g.user (views.py:10-12) and enforces nothing. The ACL predicate is inert because it is not wrapped in abort/raise. rename_file uses ensure_allowed and is correct by comparison.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. views.py:18 calls require_allowed (an alias for acl.py:4 is_allowed, which returns a bool and never aborts) as a bare statement, so its result is discarded. views.py:19 then deletes unconditionally. before_request at views.py:10-12 only sets g.user from a header and enforces nothing. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, which does abort(403)) is used only by rename_file at views.py:26, not by delete_file.
verdict.reason: All trace lines match the code: views.py:17-19 load, call, and delete with the bool discarded, and acl.py:4-5 returns a bool without aborting, so the ACL check at views.py:18 never blocks the delete. Because g.user is None when the header is absent and grants.get(None, []) yields [], even an anonymous caller reaches the delete at views.py:19.

finding.claim: Caller identity is taken from a client-supplied header with no verification, so any client can impersonate a grant holder if the header is not stripped and rewritten upstream.
finding.sink: g.user used as principal in is_allowed/ensure_allowed (views.py:18, views.py:26) and grants lookup (acl.py:5)

trace.note: before_request load_user runs on every request
g.user copied verbatim from request header
ensure_allowed grants write/rename to forged identity

finding.guards_checked: No signature, session, or token verification in this code. No proxy configuration is present in the repo, so upstream header stripping cannot be verified. Exploitable only if the app is reachable without a trusted proxy that overwrites the header.

verdict.guard_found: None in the repo verify the header. acl.py:5 is a bool check and acl.py:9-10 abort(403) on a forged identity that is in grants, so no code-level control blocks a forged identity. views.py:18 calls require_allowed (is_allowed) as a bare statement, so its bool is discarded and it enforces nothing; delete_file has no effective check at all.
verdict.reason: The cited trace is accurate (views.py:11-12 copies the header verbatim into g.user, acl.py:5 keys grants by that value, views.py:26 ensure_allowed aborts only on a grant miss), but whether an external client can actually send the header depends on upstream proxy configuration (not in the repo), so reachability cannot be decided from this code; separately, views.py:18 discards the is_allowed bool, so DELETE /files/<fid> is unguarded for any caller regardless of the header.
